definitions.gloss: to welcome in; to receive; to accept into a group
definitions.explanation: To receive someone warmly into a place, organization, or group. Combines the nuance of going out to greet (迎える) with bringing them inside (入れる).

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しいメンバーを{迎|むか}え{入|い}れた。
{留学生|りゅうがくせい}をホストファミリーとして{迎|むか}え{入|い}れる。
examples.english: To take in an exchange student as a host family.

examples.japanese: {地域|ちいき}の{人々|ひとびと}が{温|あたた}かく{迎|むか}え{入|い}れてくれたおかげで、すぐに{馴染|なじ}むことができた。
examples.english: Thanks to the warm welcome from the local people, I was able to fit in right away.

notes:
A compound verb formed from {迎|むか}える (to go out to meet, to welcome) and {入|い}れる (to put in, to let in). The combination emphasizes both the act of welcoming and the incorporation into a space or group.

ASPECT (ている):
{迎|むか}え{入|い}れている describes an ongoing state of having accepted someone into a group or place.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～を{迎|むか}え{入|い}れる (to welcome someone in)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {客|きゃく}を{迎|むか}え{入|い}れる (to welcome a guest)
- メンバーを{迎|むか}え{入|い}れる (to accept a new member)
- {難民|なんみん}を{迎|むか}え{入|い}れる (to take in refugees)
